newsitem.title: UK: New crop leads LIFFE wheat mostly up, volume thin.
newsitem.headline: New crop leads LIFFE wheat mostly up, volume thin.

text.p: LIFFE wheat ended mostly firmer in thin volume, led by the old crop.
Front month July last traded 1.00 stg higher at 78.50 stg, having seen a contract low of 77.00 stg on Monday. July volume was 76 lots of a total 321.
Tuesday was the first tender day for the July contract. A positive response to the tender helped July bounce, traders said. "People were happy to take it," one trader said.
The new crop followed the old crop, he said. There were smaller rises for new crop months. The most active wheat contract was November with 142 lots. It last traded 0.05 stg higher at 86.30 stg.
The physical market continuedto bounce along the bottom, traders said.
"It's still down there and if the currency keeps going the way it's been going I suppose it will stay down," one said.
"It seems to have bottomed," another said. He noted that the tender for the July future took some downward pressure off the market.
Brokers reported feed done for delivery in Norfolk/Suffolk in July at 82.00 stg, with barley done in the south at 81.50 for July.
